thread.title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Rise As Upbeat Corporate Updates Roll In

author: morningstar.com
title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks Rise As Upbeat Corporate Updates Roll In
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Session's big winners include AMS, Inmarsat, Novo Nordisk, Ocado
European stocks rose on Wednesday, helped by upbeat corporate updates, as many markets in the region reopened after closing for May Day.
Traders are bracing for a reading on the eurozone's first-quarter economic growth, along with reports on manufacturing and unemployment.
What are markets doing?
The Stoxx Europe 600 index was up 0.5% to 386.80, trimming its year-to-date decline to 0.6%. The pan-European index edged 0.1% lower on Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-london-sets-tone-on-may-day-holiday-2018-05-01).
The U.K.'s FTSE 100 rose 0.6% to 7,564.72, while Germany's DAX 30 tacked on 0.8% to 12,707.47. France's CAC 40 added 0.1% to 5,525.65.
The euro bought $1.2027, compared with $1.1992 late Tuesday in New York.
What is driving the markets?
Encouraging first-quarter earnings from many companies are helping to lift European equity gauges, though investors also have been worried in recent weeks about protectionism and other geopolitical flare-ups.
A softer euro has provided a boost lately to shares in Europe's export-oriented companies. Retreats for the currency, which is still up about 10% against the dollar over the past 12 months, tend to bolster the overseas revenue generated by multinational companies. The shared currency rose above $1.25 in February, but it's lately traded back around $1.20.
Check out:8 reasons to ditch the euro right now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/8-reasons-to-ditch-the-euro-right-now-according-to-b-of-a-analyst-2018-04-30)
Which economic data are in focus?
The eurozone purchasing managers' index for manufacturing in April is scheduled for release at 9 a.m. London time, or 4 a.m. Eastern Time. Economists are expecting a reading of 56, compared with 56.6 the previous month.
A preliminary reading on the eurozone's gross domestic product in the first quarter is due at 10 a.m London time, or 5 a.m. Eastern. A reading of 0.4% growth on the quarter is expected, compared with 0.6% in the last release, and 2.5% on the year, compared with 2.7%.
At the same time, an update on unemployment in the eurozone is due, expected to hold steady at a rate of 8.5%.
What are strategists saying?
"Eurozone GDP is forecast to have ticked lower to 2.5% from 2.7%," said Jasper Lawler, head of research at London Capital Group, in a note.
"Slowing growth at around 2.5% seems slightly ironic, given that it is faster than U.S. growth, and let's not talk about the U.K.'s 1.4%. However, strong growth was one of the principal factors that drove the euro higher and if that eases, then so will the euro," he said.
Stocks in focus
Shares in AMS AG (AMS.EB)rose 7% as the Austrian supplier of chips for Apple's (AAPL)iPhones appeared to catch a tailwind from the Silicon Valley giant's better-than-expected earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-were-saved-by-the-companys-new-mvp-2018-05-01) that came late Tuesday.
Read more:Shares in iPhone supplier AMS have a charge left (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-iphone-x-suppliers-stock-has-a-charge-left-even-after-tripling-this-year-2017-11-11)
And see: The surprise in Apple earnings -- big growth in China (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-surprise-in-apple-earnings-big-growth-in-china-2018-05-01)
Novo Nordisk A/S (NOVO-B.KO)posted first-quarter earnings that beat forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/novo-nordisk-earnings-beat-forecasts-2018-05-02), but the Danish pharmaceutical company cautioned that despite expecting robust sales growth in the future, intensifying competition and price pressure will have an effect. Shares jumped 4.4%.
Shares in Inmarsat PLC (ISAT.LN)gained 10% after the British satellite telecommunications company said pretax profit in the first quarter surged (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/inmarsat-profit-swings-to-net-profit-2018-05-02) versus the year-earlier period.
Ocado Group PLC's stock (OCDO.LN)climbed 5.3% after the London-listed online supermarket revealed a deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ocado-to-develop-online-platform-for-swedens-ica-2018-05-02) with Sweden's ICA Gruppen AB (ICA.SK)to develop that retailer's online grocery business. ICA shares added 1.8%.
On the downside, Paddy Power Betfair PLC's stock (PPB.DB)fell 6% after the betting company posted a drop in first-quarter profit and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/paddy-power-betfair-profit-down-to-start-buybacks-2018-05-02).
